Cable Listings and Fire Ratings: Plenum, Riser, General Purpose, Limited

Unit 2: Codes and Standards. Lesson 9 of 52 in INST1 Academy.

A pallet of cheap general-purpose cable is on sale, and the ceiling you are pulling through is an air return. Pull it and you create a violation that an inspector will find and you will pull out again.

Plenum spaces

A plenum is a space used to move air, such as a ceiling void that returns air to the air handler. Fire and smoke in a plenum spread through the entire building through the air system, so cable there must burn slowly and make little smoke.

The ratings

Rating   Name             Where it may go
CMP      plenum           air-handling spaces; highest rating
CMR      riser            vertical runs between floors, through firestopped openings
CMG/CM   general purpose  horizontal runs on one floor; not plenum, not riser
CMX      limited use      dwellings and raceways; short runs

Fiber and coax follow the same ladder: OFNP, OFNR, and OFN for nonconductive fiber, OFCP and OFCR for fiber with metal in it, and CATVP, CATVR, and CATV for coax.

The substitution rule

A higher rating can replace a lower one. A plenum cable may go in a riser or a general space; a riser cable may go in a general space. A lower rating can never replace a higher one. General cable in a plenum or riser is a violation, even for a short run.

Reading the listing

Read the jacket print. It shows the rating, the category, and the AWG. If the print is missing or unreadable, treat the cable as unrated and do not install it. The inspector reads the same print.

What the inspector checks

  • The print matches the space the cable is in.
  • Pathways and openings are firestopped.
  • Cable in a plenum is plenum rated, including cords and cable inside surface raceway.
Tip: when the ceiling above a corridor is an air return, say so on the pull schedule before cable is cut.
Exam tip: plenum (P) is above riser (R), above general (G), above limited (X). A higher rating may replace a lower one but never the reverse.
Remember
CMP beats CMR beats CMG and CM beats CMX: a higher rating may replace a lower one, never the reverse, and the jacket print tells you which you hold.
Deeper explanation

Cable Listings and Fire Ratings: Plenum, Riser, General Purpose, Limited, explained slowly

A listing table you can use

When you stand under a ceiling with a cable in your hand, you ask three things: what space is this, what rating is this cable, and is the rating at least as high as the space requires?

Cable        Rating   Plenum   Riser   General   Limited use
CMP          highest  yes      yes     yes       yes
CMR          next     no       yes     yes       yes
CMG or CM    general  no       no      yes       yes
CMX          limited  no       no      no        dwellings, raceways only

Fiber and coax follow the same order: OFNP, OFNR, OFN; OFCP, OFCR; CATVP, CATVR, CATV. The extra letter P means plenum, R means riser, and no letter means general.

Three where-may-it-go cases

Case                                        Cable in hand   Allowed?   Why
1  Pull to a drop above an air-return ceiling   CMR         no         riser is lower than plenum
2  Pull through a firestopped floor opening     CMP         yes        higher rating may replace lower
3  Run on one floor, no air handling above      CMR         yes        riser may replace general

Case 1 is the classic violation. The cable is a good cable in the wrong place. Case 2 costs more than it needs to, but it is allowed. Case 3 is legal and common when a project buys one cable for several spaces.

Worked example

A job has 40 drops in a plenum ceiling and 10 drops in a corridor with a solid ceiling and no air handling. The buyer orders CMP for the plenum and CMG for the corridor. Halfway through, the CMG runs out. Can you finish the corridor with CMP? Yes, since a higher rating may replace a lower one. Can you finish the ceiling with leftover CMG? No, since a lower rating can never replace a higher one.

What the inspector reads

The inspector reads the jacket print. A missing or faded print means the cable is treated as unrated. A cable inside surface raceway in a plenum must still be plenum rated.

Cords and small things

Patch cords and jumpers in a plenum space need plenum ratings too. A little cord in the wrong ceiling is still a violation.

Remember: P above R above G above X; higher may replace lower; the print is the proof.
